rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words ḥabb and nawā mean seed and fruit-stone.
rows.anchor: The words ﺣﺐand ﻧــﻮى mean “seed and fruit-stone.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are introduced through small things before moving to larger ones.
rows.anchor: The mention of God’s signs begins with small things and then the larger ones are referred to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits seeds and stones, drawing out their contents through stages until a plant becomes a tree, which displays His power.
rows.anchor: It is God’s power and might that is responsible to rent asunder seeds and fruit-stones

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives each seed and stone its potential and orders the earth, sky, winds, clouds, and seasons to nurture its growth.
rows.anchor: by ordering the earth, the heavens, the winds, the clouds and the seasons to play their roles and nurture them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every seed bears witness that its creator also schemed the universe as a whole.
rows.anchor: every seed that grows from this earth, by its every existence, bears witness that it has come into existence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated growth of a seed rules out independent gods governing separate domains.
rows.anchor: If this universe was being governed by different gods and they would have been independent in their own spheres

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also appears with slight variation in 6:37, where Islahi says it is explained.
rows.anchor: have been mentioned with slight variation in verse 37, where they have been explained

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes lifeless mango stones and wheat seeds producing living plants, which later yellow, decay, and wither.
rows.anchor: From the lifeless fruit-stones of mangoes and from the lifeless seeds of wheat, a luxuriant tree and a lush green plant sprouts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same recurring pattern of life and death is visible in humans and animals.
rows.anchor: The same observation can be made in human beings and animals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nations and peoples also follow a recurring rise-and-fall pattern, sometimes dominating the world before disappearing.
rows.anchor: So much so, it is the same with nations and peoples: they follow a perpetual pattern of rise and fall.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one escapes the universal law of life and death, rise and fall.
rows.anchor: No one can escape this law of life and death, rise and fall.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If another being governed the universe, it should be able to cancel this law somewhere in creation.
rows.anchor: If someone besides God was also governing this universe, why can he not annul this law in even a part of the universe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cosmos arising from matter or an unbridled force should have persisted without interruption or change.
rows.anchor: a manifestation of matter or an unbridled power, then this manifestation should have continued and perpetuated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause uses a verb depicting an occurrence, while the second uses a fāʿil form conveying decision and intent.
rows.anchor: in the first expression (bringing forth the living from the dead), a verb is used which portrays a situation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living beings do not choose death, yet nature makes every living being die; this shows that God alone has authority.
rows.anchor: once life is acquired no living being is prepared to consign itself to death but such is the relentless law of nature that every living being must die.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāqiʿah 56:86–87 similarly challenges people to restore a dying person's life if they are not subordinate.
rows.anchor: 86-87 of S ūrah al-Wāqi‘ah, it is similarly stated

rows.speaker: people
rows.claim: Some people limit the phrase to the old egg-or-hen question; Islahi reads it instead as natural laws of life and death.
rows.anchor: Generally people have confined these words to the age old question of what came first: the egg or the hen.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read with 6:102, the clause may omit its predicate, understood from the statement that God is their Lord.
rows.anchor: in the first sentence the enunciative (khabar) is suppressed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If taken as complete without ellipsis, the clause means that all this is God's benevolence, so where can people turn away?
rows.anchor: it would mean that all this is a benevolence of God; then where do you turn away.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs acknowledged God as creator of everything while still associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: everything; however, at the same time, they associated partners with Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God creates and controls everything, people should worship and obey Him alone.
rows.anchor: when all this is God’s creation and control, then people should worship Him and show obedience to Him alone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although people take an initial step toward truth, their intellect deserts them, they turn aside, and the truth they gained is lost.
rows.anchor: if they take the first step in the right direction, the next diverges from the straight path and the truth that had been gained is forever lost.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the verse concerns monotheism, the observable emergence of life from death also subtly points to resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: This verse though occurs clearly in the context of monotheism, but it also subtly points to the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If seeds and fruit-stones can emerge from earth after decay, there is no reason to wonder that humans will rise from burial.
rows.anchor: If after decaying and decomposing, seeds and a fruit-stones can once again emerge from the earth, why can’t human beings after being buried in the earth once again rise from it?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion moves from God's feats in the earth, seen in seeds and stones, to His splendor in the sky.
rows.anchor: people should also observe His splendour in the sky above them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn splitting darkness parallels God's splitting a fruit-stone to bring forth a tree.
rows.anchor: Just as He creates a tree by splitting a fruit-stone, He also brings forth the dawn after slicing through the veil of darkness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night provides comfort and rest, relieving the fatigue of the day so people can become fresh again.
rows.anchor: He has created the night to provide comfort and rest and alleviate people from tiredness of the day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-rest/day-work sequence is similarly described in al-Nabaʾ 78:9–11.
rows.anchor: In verses 9-11 of S ūrah al-Nabā, it is similarly stated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prepares people to begin their chores again by day and work for their livelihood.
rows.anchor: God sends the day after the night that people can start again with their chores and work for their livelihood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered alternation of dawn, evening, night, and day shows that they all come and go at God's command, not under different creators.
rows.anchor: all of them come and go at the behest of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After night and day, the passage turns to the two great signs appearing in them, the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: After the night and the day, the two great signs that appear in them are referred to: the sun and the moon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon precisely follow their laws and calendars, mark days, months, and years, and produce the seasons.
rows.anchor: There is a law and calendar for each of them which they minutely obey and observe and not the slightest deviate from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though in the sky, the sun and moon diligently serve earth's inhabitants without seeking praise.
rows.anchor: those who inhabit the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase draws the inference from the sun and moon's vigilance, like the call of a heart reflecting logically on the universe.
rows.anchor: depict the inference that can be drawn from the vigilance shown by the sun and the moon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon have no share in divinity; they are machinery placed and tasked by a powerful, knowledgeable God.
rows.anchor: They are like parts of a machinery fitted in their place by the powerful and knowledgeable God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe's harmony, including its opposites, testifies that one powerful, knowledgeable God governs it all.
rows.anchor: there exists amazing harmony between its opposite elements.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe is purposeful rather than amusement, and a Day of Judgement must come to manifest the Creator's wisdom.
rows.anchor: the universe has been created with a purpose which is bound to materialize.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered cosmos implies that humans should live by the Creator's directives, harmonizing their lives with the universe; this is the path to success.
rows.anchor: the Creator of human beings wants them too lead a life according to his directives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says the Qur'an also adduces prophethood from this cosmic testimony, a point he develops under 55:5.
rows.anchor: There the Qur’ān has also adduced prophethood from this testimony.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqdīr means planning.
rows.anchor: means “planning.” The attribute al-‘Az īz signifies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz denotes immense power and dominance; al-ʿAlīm denotes unfathomable knowledge encompassing wisdom.
rows.anchor: The attribute al-‘Az īz signifies His immense power and dominance and the attribute al-‘Al īm signifies His unfathomable knowledge

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is beyond the universe's system, and His power, knowledge, and wisdom embrace everything.
rows.anchor: God is not part of this system of the universe. He is above and beyond everyone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the sun and moon, attention turns to the stars as another sign serving the world's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: After the sun and the moon, attention is directed to the stars

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars' service to people testifies that the Creator deputed them for their role.
rows.anchor: they bear witness that the creator has deputed them to this
